::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## How this checkpoint works
This page mixes **quiz questions** and **mini-projects** covering all of Module 1. Try to answer without looking back at the lessons. If you get stuck, go back to the relevant lesson (linked in each section). When you are done, mark the module as complete at the bottom.

⏱️ About 30 minutes.
:::

## Part A · Quick quiz

::: {.quiz id="cp-q1"}
What does this code print?

```r
sets <- 4
reps <- 8
sets * reps
```

- [ ] `48`
- [x] `32`
- [ ] `sets * reps`

::: {.explanation}
`sets` holds 4 and `reps` holds 8, so `sets * reps` is 32. See [lesson 1.1](m1-01-basics.qmd).
:::
:::

::: {.quiz id="cp-q2"}
What is `class(c(1.5, 2, 3))`?

- [x] `"numeric"`
- [ ] `"integer"`
- [ ] `"vector"`

::: {.explanation}
A vector's class is the type of its elements. All three are (decimal) numbers, so the class is numeric.
:::
:::

::: {.quiz id="cp-q3"}
`sprints <- c(4.1, 3.9, 4.4, 4.0)`. Which code returns **only the times faster than 4.05 s**?

- [ ] `sprints < 4.05`
- [x] `sprints[sprints < 4.05]`
- [ ] `sprints[4.05]`

::: {.explanation}
`sprints < 4.05` alone gives a logical vector (`FALSE TRUE FALSE TRUE`). Putting it inside `[ ]` selects the values: `3.9 4.0`. See [lesson 1.2](m1-02-vectors.qmd).
:::
:::

::: {.quiz id="cp-q4"}
Training intensity zones are recorded as `"Z1"`, `"Z2"`, `"Z3"`. What is the best way to store them?

- [ ] As a character vector
- [ ] As a numeric vector
- [x] As an ordered factor with levels `Z1 < Z2 < Z3`

::: {.explanation}
Intensity zones are categories with a natural order, i.e. an **ordinal** variable. See [lesson 1.3](m1-03-factors.qmd).
:::
:::

::: {.quiz id="cp-q5"}
Which code selects the `minibest` scores of all **women** in `balance`?

- [ ] `balance[sex == "F", "minibest"]`
- [x] `balance[balance$sex == "F", "minibest"]`
- [ ] `balance$minibest == "F"`

::: {.explanation}
Inside square brackets you need the full column reference `balance$sex`. (With `subset(balance, sex == "F")` you could use the bare name.) See [lesson 1.4](m1-04-data-frames.qmd).
:::
:::

::: {.quiz id="cp-q6"}
In `ggplot(balance, aes(x = age, y = minibest)) + geom_point(colour = "red")`, why is `colour` outside `aes()`?

- [ ] It's a mistake: aesthetics must always be inside `aes()`
- [x] Because all points should get the same fixed colour
- [ ] Because `colour` only works for lines

::: {.explanation}
Outside `aes()` = one fixed value for all points. Inside `aes()` = the colour depends on a variable in the data. See [lesson 1.5](m1-05-ggplot.qmd).
:::
:::

::: {.quiz id="cp-q7"}
You want to compare the **distribution** of Mini-BESTest scores between three activity levels, showing every participant. Which plot is best?

- [ ] A line plot
- [ ] A histogram of all participants together
- [x] A raincloud plot with activity level on the x-axis

::: {.explanation}
A raincloud plot shows each group's distribution shape, a box plot summary and the raw data points.
:::
:::

## Part B · Mini-project: the fallers

A physiotherapist asks you: *"Do people who have fallen in the past year have poorer balance, and does that depend on age?"* Let's explore this step by step.

::: {.task}
1. Add a column `faller` to `balance` containing `"Faller"` if `falls_12m` is **1 or more** and `"Non-faller"` otherwise. (The function `ifelse(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false)` does this in one line. It's given for you.)
2. Count the participants in each combination of `faller` and `age_group` with `table()` and store it in `faller_table`.
3. Calculate the **mean Mini-BESTest score of the fallers** and store it in `mean_fallers`.
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_1
#| caption: "Mini-project · Part 1"
# 1. Faller or non-faller?
balance$faller <- ifelse(balance$falls_12m >= 1, "Faller", "Non-faller")

# 2. Cross-table of faller and age group
faller_table <- ______

# 3. Mean Mini-BESTest score of the fallers
fallers <- subset(balance, ______)
mean_fallers <- ______

faller_table
mean_fallers
```

::: {.hint exercise="cp_1"}
2. `table(balance$faller, balance$age_group)`
3. `subset(balance, faller == "Faller")`, then `mean(fallers$minibest)`
:::

::: {.solution exercise="cp_1"}
```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_1
#| solution: true
# 1. Faller or non-faller?
balance$faller <- ifelse(balance$falls_12m >= 1, "Faller", "Non-faller")

# 2. Cross-table of faller and age group
faller_table <- table(balance$faller, balance$age_group)

# 3. Mean Mini-BESTest score of the fallers
fallers <- subset(balance, faller == "Faller")
mean_fallers <- mean(fallers$minibest)

faller_table
mean_fallers
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_1
#| check: true
.check_vars(c("faller_table", "mean_fallers"), .envir_result, .checker_args$envir_solution,
  ok = "Correct! The 42 fallers have a mean Mini-BESTest score of about 19.7, compared with about 21.5 for non-fallers.")
```

::: {.task}
Now visualise it. Make a **box plot** with `age_group` on the x-axis, `minibest` on the y-axis and the boxes **filled by `faller`**. Add clear axis labels with `labs()`: x = `"Age group"`, y = `"Mini-BESTest score"`.
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_2
#| caption: "Mini-project · Part 2"
balance$faller <- ifelse(balance$falls_12m >= 1, "Faller", "Non-faller")

ggplot(balance, aes(x = ______, y = ______, fill = ______)) +
  ______() +
  labs(x = "______", y = "______")
```

::: {.hint exercise="cp_2"}
`aes(x = age_group, y = minibest, fill = faller)` + `geom_boxplot()` + `labs(x = "Age group", y = "Mini-BESTest score")`.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="cp_2"}
```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_2
#| solution: true
balance$faller <- ifelse(balance$falls_12m >= 1, "Faller", "Non-faller")

ggplot(balance, aes(x = age_group, y = minibest, fill = faller)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Age group", y = "Mini-BESTest score")
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_2
#| check: true
p <- .result
res <- .check_plot(p, geoms = "GeomBoxplot", aes = "fill")
if (isTRUE(res$correct)) {
  m <- vapply(p$mapping[c("x", "y", "fill")], function(a) if (is.null(a)) "" else rlang::as_label(a), "")
  if (!identical(unname(m), c("age_group", "minibest", "faller")))
    res <- .no("Check the aesthetics: x = age_group, y = minibest, fill = faller.")
  else if (is.null(p$labels$x) || !nzchar(p$labels$x) || identical(p$labels$x, "age_group"))
    res <- .no("Almost! Add axis labels with `labs(x = ..., y = ...)`.")
  else res <- .ok("Great work! Look closely: within each age group the boxes of fallers and non-fallers overlap a lot. Age seems to matter more than falls history. You'll learn to test this formally in Module 2.")
}
res
```

## Part C · Mini-project: your own figure

::: {.task}
Make a **scatter plot** of `age` (x) against `fes_total` (fear-of-falling score, y), with points **coloured by `sex`**, a linear trend line per sex (`geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)`), and `theme_minimal()`.
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_3
#| caption: "Mini-project · Part 3"
ggplot(balance, aes(x = ______, y = ______, colour = ______)) +
  ______ +
  ______ +
  ______
```

::: {.hint exercise="cp_3"}
`geom_point()`, then `geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)`, then `theme_minimal()`, all connected with `+`.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="cp_3"}
```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_3
#| solution: true
ggplot(balance, aes(x = age, y = fes_total, colour = sex)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal()
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: cp_3
#| check: true
p <- .result
res <- .check_plot(p, geoms = c("GeomPoint", "GeomSmooth"), aes = "colour")
if (isTRUE(res$correct)) {
  if (!grepl("theme_minimal", paste(.user_code, collapse = ""), fixed = TRUE))
    res <- .no("Nearly there. Add `theme_minimal()` as the last layer.")
  else res <- .ok("Fantastic! Surprised? In this sample, fear-of-falling scores barely change with age, and women score slightly higher than men at every age. Plotting your data is how you check your expectations. You've completed the Module 1 checkpoint!")
}
res
```
